_readme: Config for the OpenRocket CI check (or_ci.py + openrocket-sim.yml). Paths are relative to this file.
Headless OpenRocket only knows commercial motors, so team-made .rse/.eng curves must be mapped here.
Motor lookup per simulation & mount: simulations[<name>].motor(s) -> default_motor(s) -> file's own
motor -> a curve in the .ork's folder/subfolders/project folder with a matching designation -> UNRESOLVED.
motor_variants runs every simulation once per listed curve. limits {metric: {min,max}} apply per file/sim
and are written in the display units. units: metric (default) or imperial (ft, ft/s, psi); CSV/JSON stay SI.
stability_units: cal (calibers, default) or pct (% of rocket length); both are always computed, limits name
the key they mean (stability_off_rod_cal vs stability_off_rod_pct).
hide_commits {<sha>: <why>} leaves those commits out of the performance history (charts, site, CSV):
a broken or accidental save that would show as a big swing and back. 7+ hex characters, as shown on the site.
rasaero: the .CDX1 that models the same rocket. The site puts an (i) after the design's name when the two disagree
(shape, fins), and after a simulation's name when its fully loaded launch mass or CG does.
tools/openrocket/ork_vs_ras.py. rasaero_sim picks the RASAero row by motor name. Lumina and Nimitz have no RASAero model yet.
motor_files: curves a design's motors come from when no setting above names them. It does not choose a motor: each
version of the .ork still flies its own designation. It makes a change to the file a new version of the design.
Nimitz flies the Loki M3464LB booster, which OpenRocket finds itself, and the SRT K2144 sustainer from motor_files.
Full docs, metric definitions and examples: tools/openrocket/CI.md
